summary: Crossover Island Light, St. Lawrence River, NY: 1848 station of the Thousand Islands lights, discontinued 1941; island privately owned and closed.

structures.type: conical iron tower with brick lining
structures.note: LighthouseFriends gives about 30 feet (9.1 m); the Society's record gives 26 feet (7.9 m) and dates the tower to 1848
six-room, two-story; the Society's record gives 1848 and Queen Anne style

access.note: Privately owned since the 1960 surplus sale; grounds, dwelling and tower closed (LighthouseFriends). Visible from River Ledge Road and best seen from a boat.

events.note: Congress appropriates $6,000 (3 March 1847) for Crossover Island and two other Thousand Islands lights
Obed (Obediah) Robeson appointed first keeper, 15 May 1848, $350 a year
Original station: brick dwelling with wooden lantern; six oil lamps in 14-inch reflectors (LighthouseFriends)
Inspector finds the lantern room leaking and the brick poor ('soft brick'); no boathouse
Boathouse added; dwelling windows shuttered; exterior walls sheathed
Lighthouse Board requests $11,000 for a new tower and dwelling
New six-room dwelling and detached iron tower (about 30 ft) with sixth-order Fresnel lens; fourth-order lens moved to Presque Isle
Well sunk through granite, with a pump
Tower painted white at the opening of navigation (from brown)
232-foot stone and concrete seawall built on the south side
Daniel D. Hill appointed keeper, March 1909; served over twenty-two years
Keeper Daniel D. Hill takes the master of the steamer Lambert ashore by launch, 10 October; steamer had run on a shoal about a mile away
Keeper Edward J. Sweet Jr. rescues two boys from a capsized canoe, 21 June
Light discontinued 10 April 1941 and replaced with a lighted buoy
Lighted buoy takes over the light's role (LighthouseFriends)
Government sells the lighthouse as surplus property for about $6,000

wrecks.outcome: Ran on a shoal about a mile from the station; the master was brought ashore by the keeper in the lighthouse launch

corrections.why: LighthouseFriends dates the present iron tower to 1882; the 1848 light had a brick dwelling with a wooden lantern. The Society's record gives 1848 for the tower, so the record and LighthouseFriends disagree.
Sold as surplus in 1960 and privately owned since (LighthouseFriends); the record's access field already says private.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives 1882 and the Society 1848. The station's first keeper was appointed in 1848 and the first light was the 1848 brick-and-wood tower; 1882 is the date of the present iron tower.
LighthouseFriends gives 37 feet above the river for the 1848 light; the Society's record gives 34 feet. The story gives both.
LighthouseFriends has Obed Robeson; the Society's roster has Obediah Robeson. The story uses the Society's spelling and notes the other.

notes_for_editor: (1) Almost every narrative fact comes from LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; paraphrased, one short quotation per sentence). The NRHP nomination for 07001037 is not digitized on NPGallery (76-character placeholder), so the 2007 listing is not in the story. (2) The USCG Historian's page for Crossover Island appeared in a search result with 'Station Established: 1847'; it could not be read (no archived capture returned content), so that date is not used. (3) LighthouseFriends calls Ralph E. Hill the son of 'Keeper Donald D. Hill' in one place and gives the keeper as Daniel D. Hill elsewhere; the story uses Daniel D. Hill (roster and Bulletin agree). (4) The LighthouseFriends account of the 1868 inspection and the 1872 Board request is second-hand; the Board's 1872 report and the 1868 inspection were not in the local corpus. (5) The Lighthouse Service Bulletin (October 1913) was read through the corpus page; the Lambert item's surrounding paragraph was not read in full, and its year is taken from the issue date. (6) The Commissioner's 1917 list names D. D. Hill, keeper, Cross Over Island; the list's context was not read, so it is not used. (7) The record's characteristic 'Fl R 4s' (USCG Light List) conflicts with LighthouseFriends' 1848 fixed white light; the current characteristic was not checked against a current Light List, so it is left alone. (8) Private owners are not named; the 1960, 2002 and 2013 sales are given by price and year only. (9) The record's lens status is unknown; the sixth-order lens of 1882 may or may not still be in the tower. (10) The Society's record gives 1848 as the tower's establishment year, which is the original station; LighthouseFriends dates the present iron tower to 1882. The story states both. Whether the record field should read 1882 is for a human to decide (see corrections). (11) LighthouseFriends calls Ralph E. Hill the son of 'Keeper Donald D. Hill' in its footnote and gives the keeper as Daniel D. Hill in the text; the story follows the text and the Society's roster. (12) The 1872 request is quoted by LighthouseFriends from the Board's report, which was not read; the story says so. (13) The 1895, 1896 to 1897 and 1900 Board entries were read in the archive.org scan pages named in the notes; the 1896 to 1897 report's cistern is described there as 70-barrel (OCR 'wood^i 70-barrel').
